title: Introduce scenario-driven mitigation presets and telemetry-provenance tagging
author: Riley Morgan
description:
Motivation: On-call responders often follow a small set of corrective actions for recurring incident archetypes (e.g. DB connection pool exhaustion, KV cache thrash, overloaded transformer workers). This PR adds a lightweight engine to the SLO toolkit that encodes scenario-driven mitigation presets (opinionated action sets) and attaches telemetry-provenance metadata to collected snapshots so suggested mitigations are traceable to signals.

What this changes: Adds a presets registry, a runtime suggestion engine, provenance tags for telemetry snapshots, a small UI hook for the on-call HUD to preview suggested mitigations, and an opt-in safe-autofix shim that can dispatch non-destructive corrective steps (e.g. scale-up, retry-window adjustments, instance drain) behind a gate.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-1842) [x] preset registry implementation [x] provenance tags on snapshot export [x] suggestion scoring and ranking [x] opt-in safe-autofix shim with audit log [x] unit + integration tests [x] docs & migration notes [x] e2e smoke on staging

How it works (overview): The presets registry contains declarative scenario fingerprints (SLO patterns, metric thresholds, recent alert signatures) mapped to ranked mitigation recipes. When a telemetry snapshot is captured (on-call snapshot or synthetic capture), the snapshot is annotated with provenance metadata (source alert id, time-bucket, sensor-signatures) so any downstream suggestion retains a link back to the observed signals. The suggestion engine scores candidate presets against the fingerprint using a lightweight similarity heuristic (weighted metric deltas + fuzzy alert-type match). If the user has enabled the safe-autofix shim, the top-ranked non-destructive steps can be enacted via the existing orchestration adaptor with a 2-step confirmation modal and audit logging.

Rollback & safety: Safe-autofix defaults to disabled. Any enabled autofix requires: explicit team-level opt-in, a per-action rate-limit, and a two-step confirmation. All autofix actions are logged and produce an automatic revert recommendation when a stability regression is detected in the following 5 minutes window.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for preset matching and provenance formatting. Integration tests exercise snapshot tagging end-to-end and the suggestion UI hook. A staged canary on the on-call staging workspace was run for 72 hours with synthetic alerts; no regressions observed.

Related work: This complements the incident-bot's contextualizer (can be consumed as a suggestion source) and ties to the observability pack's telemetry exports for downstream analytics. Linear tasks ENG-1842 and ENG-1974 track follow-ups.

Notes: Implementation intentionally keeps preset DSL minimal to avoid ownership debates; operators can author presets via a small YAML schema documented in docs/slo/mitigation-presets.md.

notes_to_reviewers: Manual testing steps are in the PR description. impact_statement: Low-risk feature gated behind team opt-in. No schema changes to existing snapshot consumers; provenance fields are additive. Autofix defaults to off to protect production stability.
